symptom: A control probe meant to establish that a category can fire on a hand-built exemplar ran to completion and printed a well-formed result line naming a category. The one property that defined the exemplar had never actually been set on it: the runtime write that was supposed to set it had been refused. The category the probe returned was exactly what the same probe returns when that property is deliberately left unset, so the result line carried no trace of the input having failed, and the run was indistinguishable from a genuine measurement of a genuine negative.
mechanism_as_described: The probe wrote the defining property at runtime without first declaring the target predicate mutable, so the write hit a statically compiled definition and was refused with a permission error. The probe did not stop there: it went on to evaluate the exemplar, which now simply lacked the property, and the absence of that property is itself a legitimate input state that maps to a legitimate category. So the composed run produced a plausible answer instead of an error state. The failure was announced on one channel — the refusal was printed with the rest of the run's output — and completely absent from the other, and the second channel is the one a reader consumes, since the result line is what the artifact exists to record. The prose names the shape directly: a clean read identical to a read that never looked, caught one level down, at the input rather than at the output.
detection_path: The re-run added two things, and only one of them does the discriminating work. The first was the missing mutability declaration, which fixes the defect. The second was an echo of the property's actual value inside the result line itself, which is what makes the two cases separable at all — with the echo present, a run reads 'property=yes' alongside the new category, and the discarded run reads 'property=NO' alongside the old one. The artifact keeps the invalid run's output verbatim, refusal line included, immediately above the valid one, so the comparison sits on the page rather than being asserted in a sentence, and states explicitly that the finding rests entirely on the re-run.
consequence: The first run's result was discarded in full. Because the echo was added, the cost was one re-run rather than a wrong entry: without it the invalid run would have contributed a category to a cross-corpus liveness table as evidence about what the classifier does, when it was evidence about a write that never landed — and that table's purpose is precisely to decide which categories never fire anywhere, a verdict that is falsified by exactly one spurious firing or preserved by exactly one missing one. The header is written as a read-this-before-trusting-the-result preamble, i.e. the artifact carries its own validity caveat rather than leaving the reader to reconstruct it.

extraction_notes.boundary_rule_applied: UNIT — prose REPORTS an instance. The control artifact's provenance header states a specific run that occurred, what it printed, why it was invalid, and what was changed; it also pastes the invalid output. Not a discussion of the concept, even though the header generalizes the shape in one clause.
extraction_notes.selection_rule_applied: One incident per directory, fullest DESCRIBED mechanism. Extracted the invalidated control run. NOT extracted: (a) both output artifacts carry load-time warnings — a locally overridden weak import, a singleton variable, and an import of a name the exporting module does not export — which are evidence of live defects but are machine output that no prose in this directory reports or interprets; (b) the sweep document's own caveat that five categories are dark on all four corpora is explicitly withheld as not-a-verdict pending a further control, which makes it a declared open question rather than a reported incident; (c) the sweep document refers to two previously recorded incidents in other work — an identifier-reuse regime and a generation-template confound whose removal it says its own numbers corroborate. (c) is the one that could be argued: it is a report of an incident appearing in this document, but of an incident this directory did not encounter, and it carries a single line of mechanism. I did not extract it, and I flag the general question — whether a reference to an incident recorded elsewhere counts as REPORTING one — for the operator, since it bears on both strata and not just this directory.

metadata.incident_location_note: The directory's subject is a cross-corpus liveness sweep. The incident is reported in a validity header attached to one control artifact, auditing that artifact's own first run — not in the sweep document, which never mentions it.
